name: Jay Steele

tenures.source: The fed's own relaunch manifesto 'REBIRTH OF THE UEW' (msg_id cth9FV2ortYJ, 15 Mar 1997), on-screen as "President Jay"; hosts the fed's own Christmas broadcast the same year (msg_id TsgANNmNMpcJ, 25 Dec 1997); removed as president on-screen at the fed's own 1999 New Year's supercard.
tenures.note: Installed as the fed's new president the same day as the outgoing regime's final pay-per-view in March 1997; nearly two years later, on-screen at the fed's own New Year's supercard, a color commentator revealed he had bought a controlling stake in the promotion and fired him, offering a buyout in exchange for a non-voting seat on the executive committee. He left the arena to a standing ovation from the fed's own wrestlers and fans.

caption: Took over the UEW presidency on 15 March 1997, the same day as the outgoing regime's final pay-per-view, and rebuilt the fed's executive board, roleplay-decides house rule, and weekly show slate from the relaunch manifesto up.

name: Ivan Kolinski

tenures.source: Billed a former UEW Ultimate Champion in the fed's own Sunday Night Heat broadcast, 6 Apr 1997 (msg_id -fu9e7-B46YJ: "the former UEW Ultimate champion, IVAN KOLINSKI"); billed defeating Kappu for the American Championship later in 1997 (msg_id wLwmVZd3dFoJ, per the accession digest's own reading). Served as guest referee for the Ultimate Championship main event at the fed's own Ides of March 1999 pay-per-view.
tenures.note: Held both the Ultimate and American titles across 1997 in separate reigns; exact dates for either title change are not recovered here. His count as guest referee at Ides of March 1999 was called highly debatable by the fed's own broadcast.

caption: A former UEW Ultimate Champion who went on to take the American Championship from Kappu later the same year, billed on the fed's own cards as "The Crippler."

name: Professor Nickedemus Payne

tenures.source: Named a former American Champion in the fed's own relaunch manifesto (msg_id cth9FV2ortYJ, 15 Mar 1997), lost the title to Kappu "at the last Holiday Horror"; billed retaining the American Championship in a Triple Threat at Holiday Horror 2, 25 Dec 1997 (msg_id 6UlLFnrv04YJ).
tenures.note: "The Classroom," a recurring in-fiction interview segment, is hosted by this same persona per the fed's own 1996-era broadcasts (Wave T-200 dossier, the site's own captured pages) -- carried here as continuity, not independently re-verified in the 1997-99 leg.

identity.note: A same-name entity filed under the usew shard (a multi-tenure character whose Top 200 poll placement predates a usew tenure); no operator, roster, or title overlap links it to this fed's own Professor Payne.

caption: Held the UEW American Championship twice across the fed's run, losing it to Kappu at the first Holiday Horror before retaking and retaining it in a Triple Threat at Holiday Horror 2.

name: Kyle Kamikaze

tenures.source: The fed's own relaunch manifesto: reigning Television Champion as of 15 Mar 1997, having beaten both Danny Ice and Dark Destroyer in a NYC street fight, and facing Bobby Whitestar in a ladder match with the Internet title also on the line (msg_id cth9FV2ortYJ); per the accession digest's reading, later took the American Championship from Kappu in 1997. Entered the Cruiserweight Championship three-way at the fed's own Ides of March 1999 pay-per-view using a legal loophole to force his way into the match, then allowed himself to be counted out early without explanation.
tenures.note: The Internet-title ladder match happened at the fed's own Ides of March PPV the same day the manifesto was posted (msg_id 3cNontjuN_4J): Kamikaze retained the Television title and the Internet title was retired into it. His own broadcast team speculated that something was distracting him at Ides of March 1999.

identity.note: The RSPWF Top 200's own entry for this name carries no UEW tag in any edition, unlike this fed's other crossing wrestlers -- recorded distinct pending further evidence, not merged on name alone.

caption: Television Champion into the fed's March 1997 relaunch, defending the belt in a ladder match that absorbed and retired the UEW Internet Championship, then took the American Championship from Kappu later that year.

name: Bobby Whitestar

tenures.source: Billed the reigning UEW Internet Champion in the fed's own relaunch manifesto, challenging Kyle Kamikaze for both the Internet and Television titles in a ladder match (msg_id cth9FV2ortYJ, 15 Mar 1997); the title's retirement is recorded on the fed's own Ides of March broadcast the same day (msg_id 3cNontjuN_4J: "the Internet title will now be dropped from the UEW").
tenures.note: The Internet Championship's only recorded holder in this pass's corpus; the belt was retired, not lost to a successor.

caption: The UEW Internet Championship's own last titleholder, unseated when his belt was retired and unified into the Television Championship at the fed's Ides of March PPV, 15 March 1997.

name: Jeff "Madfox" Matthews

tenures.source: Billed a long-reigning UEW American Champion in the community's own 1997 RSPWF Top 200 write-up for his #18 placing -- the tag's single best community placing that year (msg_id uiktnNVnpowJ / USkiYAH5GLsJ / HASFyRJNQJ4J: "A lengthy stint at UEW American champion").
tenures.note: Also carries the MLWO, EWA, PCW and SOW fed tags in the same poll entry, an ordinary multi-fed crossover for the era; not read as identity evidence toward any of those wings.

tenures.source: Final Fight (28 November 1999): billed a former DWO, UEW and MWF star, unmasked as Sick Rick's mystery challenger and wins the DWO World Heavyweight Championship in a no-disqualification match, becoming the promotion's own last champion.
promotions/emwc/archive/an-evening-to-the-extreme-march-9-part-5-1998-03-10.html
tenures.note: At An Evening To The Extreme (9 March 1998): billed against Playboy Ronnie D, who could not wrestle and instead cut a promo claiming to have slept with Matthews' fiancee while Sean Stevens beat Matthews in SOW; Matthews walked to the ring to confront him, was struck with a folding chair by J.W. Hardin, hit with Ronnie D's crutch and given a piledriver on the chair. Lori Dane answered Todd Michaelson's jibe that he ran from the IieW by saying he had withdrawn for personal reasons.

caption: A long-reigning UEW American Champion whose title stint anchored the community's own year-end #18 ranking, the fed's best 1997 community placing.

name: Rob Magnum

tenures.source: Billed taking the Television Championship from June 1997, still champion and called the fed's "longest reigning UEW Television champion" by year end; defeated Rick Styles for the Ultimate Championship at Holiday Horror 2, 25 Dec 1997, pinning him with the finisher "Southern Comfort" (msg_id HzRR6ZDoz0AJ, read directly).
tenures.note: Held the Television and Ultimate Championships simultaneously at the held record's end point, 25 December 1997.

identity.note: A shared ring name in an unrelated fed's own roster; no operator, roster, or title overlap links it to this fed.

caption: Took the Television Championship in June 1997 and held it into the following year, then dethroned three-time champion Rick Styles for the Ultimate Championship at Holiday Horror 2 that December, still champion of both at the held record's end.

name: Kappu

tenures.source: The fed's own relaunch manifesto names him the reigning American Champion, having dethroned Professor Nickedemus Payne in a cage match at the fed's own first Holiday Horror (msg_id cth9FV2ortYJ, 15 Mar 1997); billed the American Champion entering the Ides of March Triple Threat for the Ultimate Championship the same day, read directly (msg_ids m506Ihsiq4sJ, EIQIbOggAVoJ, TP5O_irsx5cJ, OVSC6d0vaIQJ, 15 Mar 1997).
tenures.note: Eliminated first from the Triple Threat by a coin-flip interval draw; his own American Championship reign continued afterward per the wing's own reigns ledger, not independently re-read.

caption: The reigning UEW American Champion heading into the Ides of March, where he entered the Triple Threat main event for the Ultimate Championship as a title-on-title wildcard against champion Rick Styles and challenger Ivan Kolinski.

name: Alex Extreme

tenures.note: Still Television Champion at this pass's own June 1998 reading limit.

tenures.source: Deadly Draw 2 (May 1999): teams with J'ster in a submission match against Tyrone Parker and Johnny Rebel, then reaches the Deadly Rumble's final rounds. Final Fight (28 November 1999): billed "the Legend Slayer," loses a Last Man Standing Hall of Fame match to Apollo after being buried under a rigged pile of bricks.

caption: Won a four-way elimination tournament to become UEW Television Champion in February 1998 after Rob Magnum vacated the title, then retained it in a Chicago Street Fight at that year's Ides of March.

name: Mannifred Lester

identity.note: A different persona of the same name is recorded elsewhere; nothing in this federation's own record links the two.

tenures.source: Dethroned "Crippler" Ivan Kolinski for the UEW Ultimate Championship on Sunday Night Heat, 3 May 1998, locking on the Cannibal Clutch (msg_id sbHWu97L0AUJ; confirmed in the fed's own No-Action Zone recap, msg_id r-s4VuIpxcMJ, which notes he held UEW tag titles in late 1996 under the assumed name Cardiac as part of the Last Rites tag team). Lost the Ultimate Championship in an unattested defense before 1999, then re-emerged wrestling under a new name, Shimmer Glitz, in a UEW Television Championship match at the fed's own 1999 New Year's supercard.
tenures.note: Eliminated from the New Year's supercard's four-way Television Championship match by count-out, after a blindfolded ally mistook him for an opponent.

caption: Dethroned "Crippler" Ivan Kolinski with the Cannibal Clutch to become UEW Ultimate Champion in May 1998, previously known to the fed under the assumed name Cardiac of the Last Rites tag team.

name: Magnus Colby

identity.note: A different persona of the same name is recorded elsewhere; nothing in this federation's own record links the two.

tenures.note: Named on UEW's upper card in the 1997 accession digest without a tenure row of his own; this pass gives him one on the strength of his 1998 title win. Still American Champion at this pass's own June 1998 reading limit.

tenures.source: Deadly Draw 2 (May 1999): billed the promotion's own former Eastern Champion, teams with Sick Rick and Alex Martinez in a flag match, then reaches the Deadly Rumble's final four. tenures.source: Won the UEW Television Championship in a four-way match with changing five-minute stipulations at the fed's own New Year's supercard, pinning the defending champion after a blindfolded ally's mistaken interference led to a fast count-out.
tenures.note: The fed's own broadcast speculated on-air about a new alliance between him and another wrestler's manager, following his win.

tenures.source: Billed for the second night on the event's own lineup of 2 June 2002; the event was called off before it was held.

name: Chris Tyler

tenures.source: Challenged for the UEW Ultimate Championship in the fed's own New Year's supercard main event, winning by disqualification after New Alliance interference; the fed's new majority owner overruled the finish and ordered a rematch rather than hand him the title. By the fed's own Ides of March pay-per-view he is billed the reigning Ultimate Champion, retaining it in a three-way defense decided by a guest referee's disputed count.
tenures.note: Insisted on making his own entrance last at the New Year's supercard, citing a fan poll he said his own lawyer had commissioned in Japan, Mexico and America.

caption: Self-styled the UEW's real champion, he demanded to enter the ring last at the New Year's supercard, then held the Ultimate Championship into March, retaining it at Ides of March on a guest referee's disputed count.

caption: Held the UEW American Championship into the fed's own Ides of March pay-per-view, losing it back to the former champion by pinfall after a grueling defense.
